title: Metric space
summary: A metric assigns a distance satisfying nonnegativity, identity, symmetry, and the triangle inequality.

context.note: This node belongs to one explicit foundational presentation; alternate foundations may encode it differently.

assumptions.text: The declared metric geometry context is fixed.

content.plain: A metric assigns a distance satisfying nonnegativity, identity, symmetry, and the triangle inequality.
content.exact: A metric d:X×X→ℝ≥0 obeys d(x,y)=0 iff x=y, d(x,y)=d(y,x), and d(x,z)≤d(x,y)+d(y,z).
content.example: Absolute difference |x−y| is a metric on ℝ.
content.caveat: Many useful topologies are not generated by a metric.
